what_it_is.prose: The GE F404-GE-IN20 is the afterburning turbofan engine that powers Hindustan Aeronautics Limited's (HAL) LCA Tejas family of fighters — including the current Mk1A production standard that the Indian Air Force is inducting in numbers. The F404 family is an American engine from GE Aerospace (General Electric), and the IN20 variant was adapted for the Tejas application. Because India's own fighter engine — the GTRE Kaveri — never reached service readiness (a long-running DRDO/GTRE project that stalled), the Tejas line depends on the imported F404. More recently, aircraft were moved to the more powerful F404-GE-IN20/F414 family as the light fighter grew. For the Mk1A specifically, the F404-GE-IN20 (and the pathway to the larger F414 for the Mk2/AMCA) is the sole propulsion source — a structural import dependence. This matters strategically because every Tejas Mk1A delivered carries a US engine, tying the IAF's most important indigenous fighter programme to a single foreign vendor for its heart. The dependence is mitigated only by the fact that GE Aerospace is an allied supplier (US-India defence ties have deepened), but it remains a critical technology gap: India cannot yet build its own fighter engine, and the long-delayed GTRE Kaveri project is still not ready, with newer engine programmes (including a possible partnership) only at early stages.

deployments_procurement.summary: The IAF has been inducting Tejas Mk1/Mk1A fighters, all powered by the GE F404 family. The Mk1A order (a large IAF order placed in 2021) is being delivered with F404-GE-IN20 engines. The dependence is total — no Tejas has flown without a GE F404/F414 engine, and the indigenous GTRE Kaveri remains unavailable.

faq.question: What engine powers the Tejas Mk1A?
faq.answer: The LCA Tejas Mk1A is powered by a single GE F404-GE-IN20 afterburning turbofan imported from GE Aerospace (USA). The more powerful F414 powers the larger Mk2.

faq.question: Why doesn't India build its own fighter engine?
faq.answer: India's indigenous fighter engine, the DRDO/GTRE Kaveri, has been in development for decades but never reached a service-production standard, leaving the Tejas line dependent on the imported GE F404 until a viable indigenous engine matures.

faq.question: Is India trying to reduce this dependence?
faq.answer: Yes. India is pursuing licenced/co-production of GE engines (including the F414 pathway for the Mk2/AMCA) and continuing the search for an indigenous fighter-engine programme, but no fully indigenous engine is yet in service.
